summary: Fumio Enomoto specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a research assistant at Kyoto University (~1981–1985) and as a professor at Osaka University (~2000–2017).

Fumio Masutani worked in Buddhist and religious studies, earning his literature doctorate from the University of Tokyo. His career included professorships at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1952–1965) and Taisho University (~1965–1973), and serving as president of Tsuru University (1969–1971).

Fumio Ouchi specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He received his doctorate from Otani University, where he served as assistant professor (attested 1996) and later professor (attested 2014).

Fumio Shoji is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University. He has served at Rissho University as an assistant professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 2015) and later as an associate professor (attested 2026).
Fumio Tamamuro works in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Meiji University (~1956–1965) and later held a post there from circa 1978 to 2006.

Fung Kei Cheng specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Samson Tse at the University of Hong Kong, where he earned a Doctor of Philosophy (attested 2014).
Futoshi Omae is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as a lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1991) and held a post at Shimane Prefectural Junior College (attested 1997).

Futoshi Takehashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who undertook doctoral studies at Otani University (attested 1992). He served as an assistant at the Shinshu Otani-ha Institute of Shin Buddhist Studies from 1995 to 1997.
Fuyuan Luo is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He pursued a PhD at the University of Cambridge under the supervision of Adam Yuet Chau (attested 2026).

Fyodor Buslaev was a scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at the Faculty of History and Philology of Moscow University (~1834–1838) and held a post at Moscow State University in 1846.

Fyodor Shcherbatskoy was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev, Georg Bühler, and Hermann Jacobi. He was a professor at Saint Petersburg State University (~1900–1941) and founded the Institute of Buddhist Culture.

Félix Nève was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate from KU Leuven (~1834–1838) and studied under Christian Lassen, Friedrich Wilhelm Thiersch, and Eugène Burnouf. He became a professor at KU Leuven in 1841 and professor emeritus in 1877.

G. B. Palsule was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He worked as a sub-editor in the Dictionary Department at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1957) and held a post at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1987).
G. C. Nayak was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He served as a Fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study and as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research in 1996.

G. Clinton Godart works in Japanology, philosophy, and history. He completed graduate studies at the University of Chicago under James Edward Ketelaar, held postdoctoral posts at Needham Research Institute and Cambridge, and later worked at USC and Hokkaido University (attested 2017).
G. K. Jenkins worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Bloxham School and held a post at the British Museum from 1947 to 1978.

G. P. Malalasekera was an Indologist and Buddhist scholar who studied at the University of London and SOAS under Caroline Rhys Davids and William Stede. He taught at Ceylon University College and the University of Ceylon, serving as Dean of Oriental Studies.

G. Thomas Tanselle studied at Yale University. He taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1960–1978), served as vice president of the Guggenheim Memorial Foundation (1978–2006), and was adjunct professor of English at Columbia University (~1978–2006).

id: P:Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso
summary: Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso studied under both the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.

Gadjin Nagao specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, studying at Kyoto University under Ryotai Hani and Susumu Yamaguchi. He held Kyoto University's Chair of Buddhist Studies (1935–1971) and also served as a professor at Kyushu University (1956–1958).
